speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are a 34-year-old male with a history of AIDS presenting with decreased vision and floaters in your right eye. To narrow down the cause, have you noticed any pain, redness, or floaters specifically, and do you have a history of recent eye trauma or surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. Given your history of AIDS, recent fungal esophagitis treatment, and Kaposi's sarcoma, along with painless floaters and vision loss in one eye, this is the most likely cause. Please request a dilated fundus examination immediately to confirm retinal hemorrhages and necrosis.
